entries.title: Oil Platforms (Islamic Republic of Iran v United States of America)
entries.principle: The use of force in self-defence must be necessary and proportionate; a State may not rely on self-defence where the necessity is not established.
entries.facts: Iran claimed that the United States unlawfully attacked Iranian oil platforms.
entries.holding: The use of force in self-defence must be necessary and proportionate; a State may not rely on self-defence where the necessity is not established.

entries.title: Articles on Responsibility of States for Internationally Wrongful Acts
entries.citation: ILC Articles on Responsibility of States for Internationally Wrongful Acts (2001) UN Doc A/56/49(Vol I)/Corr 4
entries.principle: Every internationally wrongful act entails responsibility; conduct is attributable where an organ acts, or where instructions, direction or control are exercised; reparation must wipe out the consequences of the wrong.

entries.title: Gabčíkovo-Nagymaros Project (Hungary v Slovakia)
entries.principle: Necessity may preclude wrongfulness only in exceptional circumstances; a State may not rely on changed circumstances to evade a treaty obligation, and good faith governs performance.
entries.facts: A dispute over a dam project on the Danube between Hungary and Slovakia.
entries.holding: Necessity may preclude wrongfulness only in exceptional circumstances; a State may not rely on changed circumstances to evade a treaty obligation, and good faith governs performance.

entries.title: Military and Paramilitary Activities in and against Nicaragua (Nicaragua v United States of America)
entries.principle: A State is responsible where it exercises effective control over non-State actors; the prohibition on the use of force and the principle of non-intervention are rules of customary international law.
entries.facts: Nicaragua claimed that the United States was responsible for military and paramilitary activities against it.
entries.holding: A State is responsible where it exercises effective control over non-State actors; the prohibition on the use of force and the principle of non-intervention are rules of customary international law.
entries.judges: Nagendra Singh, President (International Court of Justice)

entries.title: North Sea Continental Shelf (Federal Republic of Germany v Denmark; Federal Republic of Germany v Netherlands)
entries.principle: Customary international law requires both widespread and representative State practice and opinio juris; treaty provisions do not automatically crystallise into custom.
entries.facts: A dispute over the delimitation of the continental shelf in the North Sea.
entries.holding: Customary international law requires both widespread and representative State practice and opinio juris; treaty provisions do not automatically crystallise into custom.

entries.title: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties
entries.citation: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (adopted 23 May 1969, entered into force 27 January 1980) 1155 UNTS 331
entries.principle: A treaty is interpreted in good faith in accordance with the ordinary meaning of its terms, in their context and in light of its object and purpose; travaux préparatoires are supplementary only.
